seams.title: Registry schema: checker spec and published file
seams.must_agree: The published JSON Schema is the exact output of the checker's SCHEMA.
seams.consequence: A tool that reads seams.json through the published schema accepts entries the checker refuses, or refuses entries it accepts.

seams.title: Release version
seams.must_agree: The package, the plugin and the checker state the same version.
seams.consequence: The copy warning in `seams check` compares the wrong numbers, so a repo can run an old checker without notice.

seams.title: Commands the docs name
seams.must_agree: Every `seams <command>` the docs name exists in the CLI.
seams.consequence: An agent following the skill runs a command that does not exist.

ties.note: Checks that the docs name only real commands. It does not check that every command is documented.

seams.title: Reviewer output format: brief and merge
seams.must_agree: The JSON example in the reviewer brief has exactly the fields the merge accepts.
seams.consequence: Reviewer agents write a field the merge rejects, so the merge skips their seams.

seams.title: Drift check output format: brief and collector
seams.must_agree: The JSON example in the drift check brief has exactly the fields the collector accepts.
seams.consequence: Drift checkers write a field the collector rejects, so their findings are dropped.

seams.title: Merge report sections the skill tells the user to settle
seams.must_agree: Every section name that step 5 of the seams-review skill bolds is in merge.SETTLE, and merge.py writes a section with that name.
seams.consequence: The skill sends the user to a section the report never writes, and the user cannot tell an empty section from a renamed one.
